title: ordinal
summary: Create an ordinal categorical array object.

gpu_support.notes: Ordinal categorical arrays are host metadata objects.

description: `ordinal(A)` creates a categorical object whose categories are ordered. It is a compatibility constructor equivalent to `categorical(..., 'Ordinal', true)`.
behaviors: String, char, cellstr, numeric, and logical inputs are accepted through the same label conversion path as `categorical`.
`ordinal(A)` derives sorted unique categories from non-missing labels.
`ordinal(A, categories)` uses the supplied category order and marks labels not present in that list as missing.
`ordinal(A, valueset, catnames)` maps source values through `valueset` and stores the corresponding category names from `catnames`.
The returned object has class `categorical`, stores one-based category codes, and has its `Ordinal` metadata flag set to true.
Equality and relational operators compare category order; categorical-to-categorical comparisons require matching category lists.

`min` and `max` reduce ordinal categorical arrays by category order and return categorical results; undefined elements follow the numeric `NaN` behavior of `includenan` and `omitnan`, and multi-output forms return numeric indices.

faqs.question: How is `ordinal` different from `categorical`?
faqs.answer: `ordinal` always sets the categorical `Ordinal` flag to true, so category order is meaningful for compatibility code that checks ordinal categorical metadata.
